findings.reason: the node dispatched to §3 would edit a function that lacks the declarations its rule turns on, and would have to move or re-signature it before its own done-when fixtures could pass.
findings.text: §3 says "The change is one edit to the blocker function ... `unpassed_gate_blockers` in `reckon/lifecycle.py`", but that function is `unpassed_gate_blockers(gates: list[dict[str, Any]])` (`reckon/lifecycle.py:52`) and takes only gate rows, none of which carries its gated section's declaration, so it cannot decide "an open gate whose gated sections are all done, descoped or deferred"; that decision lives in `split_unpassed_gates` (`reckon/roadmap.py:807`), which holds `implementable_sections(plan["section_declarations"])` and returns the plan-holding half of the split, and it is the function every consumer reaches (`reckon/roadmap.py:3200`, `reckon/mcp_views.py:2504`, `reckon/serve.py:1924`)

findings.reason: §3's "every reader of gate blocking already calls it" is the premise of its single-edit argument, and a caller that does not resolve leaves that premise unverifiable.
findings.text: §3 names "the MCP through `_plan_gate_blockers` in `reckon/mcp_views.py`"; no such symbol exists (`grep -rn _plan_gate reckon/` returns nothing), and the MCP reader that does exist, `_section_gate_blockers` (`reckon/mcp_views.py:2504`), reports only the section-scoped half of `split_unpassed_gates` and not the plan-holding half §3's rule concerns

findings.reason: the fixture's stated base arm is its negative control, so a node would encode `deferred` as the base and then contend with a base that returns `blocked` when its test runs.
findings.text: §2's second done-when fixture ("every section done, an open execution gate and no open followup ... where the base reads it `deferred`") asserts a base reading the ladder cannot produce: with every section done there is no implementable section, so `split_unpassed_gates` returns the open gate in the plan-holding list (`reckon/roadmap.py:812-813`), `is_blocked` is then true and readiness reads `blocked` (`reckon/roadmap.py:3261-3269`) — the same shape §1 itself describes as "`blocked` at 100 %", not deferred

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §3 cites a caller in `reckon/mcp_views.py` that no longer exists; every other symbol, file and section named across s2–s5 resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's second fixture states its base arm reads `deferred`, a reading no code path produces; each of s2, s3, s4, s5 otherwise names a control and a base arm that fails.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the census evidence is on `docs/evidence/archive/a-finished-plan-closes-landed.html` (present), and each section's gate is a pytest fixture under `tests/`, neither a scratchpad nor a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, filename or comment in s2–s5; the only plan names in the prose name other plans, which prose may do.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §3 places its rule in a function that cannot see the input the rule needs, so the stated mechanism does not run on the stated path.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 (s2) carries the closable readiness plus the closure_blockers widening as one change to the same payload, §3–§5 each name one deliverable, and §6 one.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` declares s4→`a-project-reads-as-one-picture#s9`, s5→`a-finished-plan-closes#s2` and s6→s2,s3,s4,s5; every declared edge resolves, and the cited plan/section anchors (`a-project-reads-as-one-picture` §7 and §9, `a-sprint-closes-on-completable-work`, `docs/evidence/archive/a-finished-plan-closes-landed.html`) all exist.
